Sadly I predict more of this happening over time. Open Source is a good idea in some scenarios and applications like OSes and the software that drives the internet but it has left huge gaping holes in the business and government sectors. FOSS projects focus on a specific set of tools and applications and often revolve around entertainment and media so many programmers flock to those projects and ignore others that are mundane or boring. Businesses have little available to them in the off the shelf catalog of open source software and are required to develop the software they need of buy it from closed source vendors who saw the opportunity to fill a gap. The large pool of .Net and other Microsoft technology developers found around the world make it easier to find talent to build custom applications than someone who is skilled in the FOSS development world who isn't switching distros, languages, tool chains and ideologies on a weekly basis. Businesses and government organizations need things to be relatively unchanging over time yet flexible enough to meet there needs. Sadly for the FOSS world they have not met those basic needs and Microsoft has a long history of winning at that. The FOSS world needs to get realistic and start acting like a closed source company if it is to gain the discipline and maturity needed to address these shortcomings. We have some of that in the Linux kernel being controlled rather tightly but we need to lock down other areas to avoid the constant reinventing of the proverbial wheels on a daily basis if FOSS is to succeed long term in business. I hope we can find the right formula to make that work in the future but I just don't see it happening in this fragmented open source community we have today.

MS is always the scapegoat for FOSS not maturing and evolving but the reality is they are not the true cause. Every distro released is an example of one group's dissatisfaction with another's work and just adds to the pile of "choice" that end users must wade through to find what meets their needs today and in the future. The churn that happens from changing distros when projects go stale or abandoned only makes this more frustrating. Sure Windows 10 is a disaster, but prior to Satya Nadella driving the company into this disaster, Microsoft was on the way to being great again. }
